clue.text: Finish off Kent town's wine

indicators.note: off says the word for finish is taken away from the town's name

parts.note: Gravesend is a town in Kent on the Thames estuary; the 's stands for 'is'
a finish is an end

explanation.surface: Someone orders a bottle of the local wine to round off a visit to a Kent town.
explanation.walkthrough: GRAVESEND is a town in Kent, England; 'off' removes END ('Finish') from it.
explanation.definitionFit: Graves is a red or white wine from the Bordeaux region of France, named after its gravelly soil.

clue.text: Upright type of horse that covers miles

indicators.note: the horse word goes round the abbreviation, covering it

parts.note: a roan is a horse with a coat of mixed colours

explanation.surface: A question about what kind of horse carries a rider over many miles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upright type' is printing: roman letters stand up straight, unlike italic.
explanation.definitionFit: In typography, roman is the ordinary upright typeface as opposed to slanting italic.

clue.text: Retaliation against English heading from Europe supported by two thirds of France

indicators.note: in a down clue the last piece sits underneath, holding up the rest

parts.note: V, short for versus, means against

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter
four of the six letters of the country's name are kept, dropping the first two

parts.note: the country's name, trimmed

explanation.surface: A political story: Britain hits back against Europe, backed by most of France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two thirds of France' keeps four of its six letters, ANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Vengeance is punishment inflicted in return for a wrong, which is what retaliation means.

clue.text: Some Aussies take a rest when it's hot

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Australians, living in a hot climate, are said to take an afternoon nap.
explanation.definitionFit: A siesta is an afternoon nap taken in hot countries during the warmest part of the day.

clue.text: 99 perhaps emerging from church in America mostly bewildered

indicators.note: bewildered means confused, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: mostly means all but the final letter

parts.note: the name with its last letter cut

explanation.surface: A bewildered American emerging from church holding a cone on a hot day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'emerging from' and 'in' are link words: CE plus AMERIC (America 'mostly') are rearranged. A 99 is a British soft ice-cream cone with a chocolate flake stuck in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A 99 is one example of a cone of soft-serve dessert, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Cover used for a leaking roof ?

definitions.text: Cover used for a leaking roof ?

parts.words: Cover used for a leaking roof ?
parts.note: cover in the financial sense: a householder claims for repairs to a leaking roof under this document, not under a tarpaulin

explanation.surface: Something to throw over a roof that lets in rain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cover' suggests a sheet or tarpaulin; it is financial cover, which pays for the damage.
explanation.definitionFit: A householder's financial protection contract pays out for damage such as a leaking roof.

clue.text: Group seen excitedly describing new mobile regularly ignored

indicators.note: describing in its old sense of drawing round, so one set of letters encircles the other
excitedly means in an agitated way, so the letters are jumbled
every other letter of the words is skipped, keeping the alternate ones

explanation.surface: A band excitedly describing the new mobile phone they have seen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describing' is used in the old sense of drawing a line round; the anagram of SEEN is ENSE, and 'regularly ignored' keeps the even letters of 'new mobile'.
explanation.definitionFit: An ensemble is a group of musicians or performers who play together.

clue.text: Swift attack captures leader of pirates

indicators.note: captures means takes in, so the attack word holds the letter

parts.note: a raid is a sudden attack

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Pirates mount a quick assault and seize their own captain.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapid and swift are synonyms, both meaning very fast.

clue.text: Abolition of bishops possibly defended by woman during last month

parts.note: Ann is a woman's name

indicators.note: being defended by something means being surrounded by it, so the outer pieces enclose the chessmen

parts.note: ULT, short for ultimo, means in or during last month in old business letters
bishops are chessmen, one example of men on a board

explanation.surface: Bishops faced being abolished last month, with a woman defending them.
explanation.walkthrough: Bishops are chess pieces, so 'bishops possibly' is a definition by example; 'defended by' signals one piece enclosed by others.
explanation.definitionFit: An annulment is the cancelling of a law or marriage, which is a kind of abolition.

clue.text: Secretary of a football club being Swiss is oddly overlooked

parts.note: Man U is short for Manchester United football club

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters are passed over, keeping the even ones

explanation.surface: The secretary of a football club turns out to be Swiss and is strangely ignored.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the odd letters of 'being Swiss' leaves ENSIS; 'is' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: An amanuensis is a literary assistant who takes dictation or copies manuscripts, a type of secretary.

clue.text: Knock leg against edge of rock

parts.note: pins is slang for legs

indicators.note: the edge here is the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A climber bangs a leg against the edge of a rock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knock' is the engine sense: pinking is the metallic knocking of a car engine, so 'Knock' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: An engine is said to pink when it makes a rattling knock from badly timed ignition.

clue.text: Son for second new father is an angel

indicators.note: the son's letter takes the place of the second occurrence of the new letter

parts.note: the father of an idea is the person who devised it

explanation.surface: A newborn son replacing a new father, who turns out to be an angel.
explanation.walkthrough: INVENTOR has two Ns; 'for second' swaps the second N for S. An angel in theatre is a financial backer of a show.
explanation.definitionFit: In theatre slang, an angel is a backer who puts money into a production.

clue.text: Where to find hotel in Cleethorpes?

definitions.text: Where to find hotel in Cleethorpes?

parts.words: Where to find hotel in Cleethorpes?
parts.note: hotel is H in the phonetic alphabet, and in the eleven-letter word Cleethorpes that letter sits sixth, exactly central

explanation.surface: A visitor asks where they can find a hotel in a seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: Cleethorpes is a seaside resort in Lincolnshire, England; Hotel is the radio code word for H.
explanation.definitionFit: The letter H sits at the centre point of the town's name, with five letters on each side.

clue.text: Babies want to hold a pen for instance

indicators.note: to hold says the words contain the answer in their letters

explanation.surface: Toddlers keep reaching to grab a pen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pen' is the female swan, not a writing tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen is a female of this large white water bird, so it is one example of the species.

clue.text: Sport involving power a lot

indicators.note: to involve originally meant to roll up or entangle, so the letters are twisted round

explanation.surface: A sport that demands a great deal of strength.
explanation.definitionFit: Water polo is a team ball game played by swimmers in a pool.

clue.text: Live around extensive outskirts of Exeter? Not any more

indicators.note: around means turned about, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: on means live, as a switched-on circuit or a show that is on
long means extensive

indicators.note: the outskirts are the outermost letters

explanation.surface: Someone who used to live on the outskirts of Exeter has moved.
explanation.walkthrough: Exeter is a city in Devon, England.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means formerly but not now, the same as not any more.

clue.text: State of recently born calf

parts.note: something recently born is new
a Jersey is a breed of dairy cattle, so a calf might be one

explanation.surface: A question about the condition of a newborn calf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like condition; it is a US state. Jersey cows come from the Channel Island of Jersey.
explanation.definitionFit: This is one of the fifty states of the USA, on the east coast.

clue.text: Discrimination acceptable within Florida? Charming!

parts.note: taste is discrimination in matters of style

indicators.note: within puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: FL is the postal abbreviation for Florida
U means acceptable, upper-class usage

explanation.surface: A sarcastic reaction to discrimination being thought acceptable in Florida.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charming!' is usually an ironic retort, but here it is taken straight. U means upper-class or socially acceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done in good style is pleasing and elegant, so charming in a literal sense.

clue.text: See great changes in government

indicators.note: changes means alters, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An observer notices big shifts in how the country is run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word. 'government' is used in its old sense of steering or directing.
explanation.definitionFit: Steerage once meant direction or guidance, and government also meant steering, as of a ship.

clue.text: Pardon announced for engineer

indicators.note: announced means spoken, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: What? is a blunt way of saying Pardon? when you mishear

explanation.surface: A pardon is announced for an engineer.
explanation.walkthrough: James Watt was the Scottish engineer who improved the steam engine.
explanation.definitionFit: James Watt was the eighteenth-century Scottish inventor whose name became the unit of power.

clue.text: Wisteria at last slowly envelops shed

indicators.note: envelops means wraps round, so the slow word encloses the letter

parts.note: lento is the musical direction for slowly

indicators.note: at last means the final letter

explanation.surface: A climbing plant slowly grows until it covers a garden shed.
explanation.definitionFit: A lean-to is a small shed or outbuilding built against a wall with a sloping roof.

clue.text: Quick pint following concert

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the pint abbreviation comes second

parts.note: a prom is a promenade concert, as at the BBC Proms

explanation.surface: A quick pint at the bar after the concert.
explanation.walkthrough: The Proms are the BBC's summer season of classical concerts in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Prompt means done without delay, which is a synonym for quick.

clue.text: Number historically entering medicine got together socially

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so the number goes into the medicine word

parts.note: the Romans wrote nine as IX

explanation.surface: A historical number of doctors met up for drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'historically' tells you to use Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: To mix is to socialise or mingle with others, so the past tense means got together socially.

clue.text: Dish of duck, made without stuffing, left by setter essentially

parts.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, shown by the letter O

indicators.note: the inner letters are removed, leaving the outside pair
essentially means at its core, the middle letters

explanation.surface: A recipe for duck made with no stuffing, left by the cook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setter' looks like a cook; it is the crossword setter. 'Dish of duck' misleads: 'of' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: An omelette is a dish of beaten eggs cooked in a pan.

clue.text: Clichéd term receives immense television exposure initially

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of each word

explanation.surface: A tired phrase becomes even more tired after enormous TV exposure.
explanation.definitionFit: Trite means overused and lacking originality, the same as clichéd.

clue.text: Trick central characters in show with source of audience vote

indicators.note: the central characters are the middle letters of the word
the source is the opening letter

parts.note: X is the cross marked on a ballot paper to vote

explanation.surface: A TV talent show rigs its audience vote.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoax is a deception or practical joke, a kind of trick.

clue.text: Without a stir, African winds up joint company

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the following letters are taken away from the word

parts.note: the word as written, with letters removed
stir and can are both slang for prison
winds up means finishes, as a speaker ends
the hip is a joint of the body

explanation.surface: An African calmly closes down a joint business venture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' removes A and CAN from AFRICAN to leave FRI. The obvious first try is an anagram of STIR AFRICAN signalled by 'winds up'; 'winds up' is a synonym for ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Friendship and company both mean companionship, as in enjoying someone's company.

clue.text: Repartee's rank over lady confused about parking

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', so the definition reads as repartee

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a row is a rank or line

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the jumbled letters go round the parking letter
confused means mixed up, so the letters are shuffled

parts.note: P is the symbol for parking

explanation.surface: Banter about a muddled lady parking her car.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'over' turns the word backwards, giving WOR; 'confused' rearranges LADY as DLAY, which 'about' puts round P.
explanation.definitionFit: Clever witty exchange is both repartee and the playful use of words.

clue.text: Element evenly distributed throughout Kosovo?

parts.note: the chemical symbol O fills every even-numbered place in the word Kosovo: second, fourth and sixth

explanation.surface: A chemical element found spread across a Balkan country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evenly' is taken literally: the even letters of Kosovo are all the symbol O.
explanation.definitionFit: This gas is the chemical element whose symbol is the single letter O.
